mainTopic: Which תמיד 'לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד' refers to; warming the כהן גדול's מקוה with heated iron and דבר שאין מתכוין; the second טבילה in בית הפרוה and the cost of the white garments
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about the verse 'לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד'. רבנן say it speaks of the afternoon תמיד, so the morning תמיד is learned from it. רבי says the reverse. רבה בר עולא explains רבי's source: 'the one lamb' points back to the lamb already called 'one', which is the morning תמיד. The גמרא then shows how each side learns that an offering must be the best animal, from 'אחד' and from 'ומבחר נדריך'. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה about warming the מקוה for an old or delicate כהן גדול. רבי יהודה says heated iron blocks were dropped into the water. To the question of whether this hardens the iron, רב ביבי answers that the iron never got hot enough. אביי answers that even if it did, a דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted, because hardening iron is only a rabbinic prohibition, so even רבי יהודה allows it. Finally, a new משנה describes the כהן גדול's second טבילה in בית הפרוה and the value of his white linen garments.

steps.title: רבי says the afternoon offering is learned from the morning one
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees with רבנן and holds that the evening תמיד is learned from the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: the evening offering is learned from the morning offering.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a ברייתא. Here רבי gives his opinion against רבנן about which daily offering is the source for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן held that the verse 'לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד' speaks about the afternoon תמיד, so the morning תמיד is learned from it. רבי flips this: the verse speaks about the morning תמיד, and the afternoon תמיד (ערבית) is learned from it (משל שחרית).

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
The evening offering is learned from that of the morning.
phrases.notes: The opposite of what רבנן said earlier in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the position of רבנן stated on the previous amud in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי, the verse 'לכבש האחד' refers to the morning תמיד, and the afternoon תמיד is derived from it.

steps.title: Asking for רבי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands רבנן's view, since the verse sits in the section on the afternoon תמיד, but asks what רבי's reasoning is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבנן, because this verse is written about the afternoon offering. But רבי, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבנן's view is easy to understand, and then asks why רבי reads the verse differently. This sets up the next step, where רבי's source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By its location, the verse appears to be talking about the afternoon תמיד, which supports רבנן. So רבי needs a reason to say it actually refers to the morning one.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בְּתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם כְּתִיב.
phrases.english: this verse is written about the afternoon daily offering.
But Rabbi, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבי's statement in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What textual basis does רבי have for applying the verse to the morning תמיד?

steps.title: The word 'one' points back to the morning offering
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא explains that 'לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד' means 'the lamb that was already called אחד', and that is the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: The verse says 'for the one lamb.' Which lamb was described as 'one'? You must say it is the morning daily offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא gives רבי's source. The phrase 'the one lamb' points back to a lamb that the Torah already called 'one'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the Torah said 'אֶת הַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד תַּעֲשֶׂה בַבֹּקֶר', using 'one' for the morning lamb. So 'לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד' refers back to that morning lamb, even though the verse appears near the afternoon one.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say / it must be

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
The verse says: 'For the one lamb.'
Which lamb is the one about which 'one' was said?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר זֶה תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר.
phrases.english: You must say: this is the morning daily offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The definite 'the one lamb' refers to the lamb earlier labeled 'one', which is the morning תמיד.

steps.title: How רבנן read the word 'one'
steps.stepSummary: רבנן read 'אחד' as 'the choicest of its flock', a requirement of quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן: what does 'one' mean? The special one in its flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבנן explain the word 'אחד' if they do not use it like רבי, and answers that it teaches the lamb must be the best of the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבנן do not read 'one' as pointing to the morning lamb, the word needs a different meaning. They take it as 'unique', meaning a top-quality animal.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: what is 'one'?
The special one in its flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word that רבי used as his source, according to רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אחד' teaches that the תמיד must be the choicest animal of the flock.

steps.title: רבי learns the best-animal rule from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי derives the requirement of choice animals from 'וּמִבְחַר נְדָרֶיךָ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי: he learns it from 'and the choicest of your vows.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי gets the rule that an offering must be top quality, since he used 'אחד' for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not lose the best-animal rule. He simply learns it from a different verse, 'ומבחר נדריך' in דברים.

keyTerms.meaning: The choicest of your vow-offerings (דברים יב:יא)

phrases.english: And Rabbi?
He derives it from 'and the choicest of your vows.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי's source for the rule that רבנן derived from 'אחד'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי learns the quality requirement from 'ומבחר נדריך'.

steps.title: רבנן need both verses
steps.stepSummary: רבנן use one verse for obligatory offerings (חובה) and one for voluntary offerings (נדבה), and both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן: one is for obligatory offerings and one is for voluntary offerings, and both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבנן need both 'אחד' and 'ומבחר נדריך': each teaches the best-animal rule for a different kind of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one verse, we might limit the rule to one type. It might apply only to obligations, or only to gifts, since a poor gift might be better not brought at all. So רבנן need one verse for חובה and one for נדבה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי: 'לכבש האחד' is the morning תמיד, and the best-animal rule comes from 'ומבחר נדריך'. רבנן: the verse is the afternoon תמיד, 'אחד' means the choicest, and both verses are needed, one for חובה and one for נדבה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
One is for obligatory offerings and one is for gift-offerings,
and both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבנן still need 'ומבחר נדריך' after learning the rule from 'אחד'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One verse covers חובה and one covers נדבה, and neither could be learned from the other.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: an old or delicate כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about warming the מקוה for an old or sensitive כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן גדול was old or delicate, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that for a weak כהן גדול, hot water was added to his cold immersion water. The גמרא will now explain how this was done.

phrases.english: If the High Priest was
old or delicate, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל זָקֵן אוֹ אִיסְטְנִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. The גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an old or delicate כהן גדול, the cold מקוה water was warmed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: heated iron blocks warmed the water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה says iron blocks were heated on ערב יום הכפורים and placed into the cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said: They would heat blocks of iron on ערב יום הכפורים and throw them into the cold water so that its chill would ease.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains a different method of warming the water. Iron blocks were heated the day before and dropped into the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heating was done on ערב יום הכפורים, so no fire was used on the holy day. But dropping hot iron into cold water on יום הכפורים itself will raise a question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
They would heat blocks of iron
from Yom Kippur eve
and throw them into the cold water,
so that its chill would ease.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה describes a different warming method (heated iron blocks) from the משנה's hot water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Iron blocks heated on ערב יום הכפורים were cast into the cold water on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Doesn't this harden the iron?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that dropping hot iron into cold water hardens it, which is a forbidden מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he harden the iron?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that cooling red-hot iron in water hardens (tempers) it. This is a forbidden act on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quenching hot metal in water strengthens it. That counts as finishing a utensil (צירוף), so throwing the iron in seems to be a forbidden מלאכה.

phrases.english: But doesn't he harden the iron!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method described in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ברייתא permitting iron blocks to be cast into water on יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Quenching hot iron hardens it, which is a forbidden מלאכה on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רב ביבי: the iron never got that hot
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי answers that the iron was not heated to the temperature where quenching hardens it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said: It did not reach the point of hardening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי answers the question by saying the blocks were only warmed. They were not heated enough for the water to harden them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hardening only happens if the metal is extremely hot. Since these blocks were only meant to take the chill off, no צירוף happens at all.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said:
It did not reach the point of hardening.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the iron was hot enough to be hardened.
steps.terutzMaskana: The iron was only mildly heated, so no hardening happens.

steps.title: אביי: an unintended result is permitted
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even if the iron did harden, the person casting it in did not intend that, and a דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if you say it reached the point of hardening, an act one does not intend is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer. Even if the iron did get hot enough, the person only wanted to warm the water, so the hardening is an unintended side effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not limit the case like רב ביבי. He invokes the principle that a forbidden result one does not intend (דבר שאין מתכוין) does not make the act forbidden. The goal here was warm water, not stronger iron. Because the ברייתא is in the name of רבי יהודה, step 12 will ask whether רבי יהודה accepts this principle.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers on the iron blocks. רב ביבי says the iron never reached hardening temperature. אביי says even if it did, it is a דבר שאין מתכוין, which is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the iron does not harden. He agrees it may harden, but holds that an unintended result is permitted. That is a different answer from רב ביבי's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step applies the major principle of דבר שאין מתכוין מותר to a case in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if you say it reached the point of hardening,
an unintended act is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְצֵירוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא, without relying on רב ביבי's limitation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hardening would forbid the act even though it was not the goal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if the iron hardens, the act is permitted because the hardening was not intended.

steps.title: Did אביי really permit an unintended act according to רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. In another place, אביי himself explained that רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did אביי really say this? But we learned in a ברייתא: "the flesh of his foreskin" teaches that even if there is a בהרת (a white leprous spot) there, he may cut it off. These are the words of רבי יאשיה. And we asked about this: why do I need a verse to permit it? And אביי said: the verse is needed according to רבי יהודה, who said that a דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer from step 11 by quoting another statement of אביי that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, אביי said that רבי יהודה (the author of the iron ברייתא) permits an unintended act. But in the case of מילה on a spot with a בהרת, אביי explained that a special verse was needed because רבי יהודה forbids unintended acts. So אביי seems to contradict himself about רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A white leprous spot of צרעת. The Torah forbids cutting it off.
His foreskin (from the verse about מילה)
"And we discussed it": the גמרא is recalling an earlier discussion
"Why do I need a verse?": the גמרא asks why a verse is needed for something that seems obvious

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not giving his own personal opinion in either place. In both places he is explaining the view of רבי יהודה. That is exactly why there seems to be a contradiction.

phrases.english: And did Abaye really say this?
phrases.notes: This refers to אביי's answer in step 11, that an unintended act is permitted.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita: "the flesh of his foreskin"
phrases.notes: ויקרא יב:ג, about the מצוה of מילה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם בַּהֶרֶת — יָקוֹץ,
phrases.english: even in a place where there is a leprous white spot, he may cut
phrases.notes: Normally it is forbidden to cut off a sign of צרעת.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.
And we discussed it: why do I need a verse?
phrases.notes: He only intends to do the milah, not to remove the spot.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: it is according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: an unintended act is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This seems to contradict what אביי said about the iron blocks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in step 11 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that according to רבי יהודה, placing the hot iron is permitted because the hardening is unintended.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere אביי says רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין. That is why the verse was needed to permit מילה on a בהרת. So he cannot also say that רבי יהודה permits it here.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids unintended acts only for Torah prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין only when the prohibition is from the Torah. Hardening the iron is only rabbinic, so here it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies to the whole Torah, meaning Torah prohibitions. But here, hardening the iron is only a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by limiting where רבי יהודה's strict rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule forbidding a דבר שאין מתכוין applies to Torah-level prohibitions, like cutting a בהרת. Hardening iron by dipping it in water is only forbidden מדרבנן. For a rabbinic prohibition, even רבי יהודה agrees an unintended act is permitted. So אביי does not contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: "These words apply…": introduces a limit on a rule
The whole Torah, meaning Torah-level prohibitions
Hardening (tempering) hot metal by putting it in water

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין only for Torah prohibitions. For a rabbinic prohibition, like hardening the iron here, it is permitted. So heating the מקוה water for the כהן גדול is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that how strict we are about an unintended act can depend on whether the prohibition is from the Torah or from the רבנן.

phrases.english: That applies to the whole Torah (Torah prohibitions),
but here, the hardening is only rabbinic.
phrases.notes: So even רבי יהודה permits the unintended act here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: Torah prohibitions versus rabbinic prohibitions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה forbids every unintended act, so אביי seemed to contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה forbids an unintended act only for Torah prohibitions. Hardening iron is rabbinic, so it is permitted.

steps.title: The second immersion in בית הפרוה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes how the כהן גדול immersed a second time in בית הפרוה. It also brings a מחלוקת about whether he washed his hands and feet before or after undressing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: They brought him to בית הפרוה, which was in the holy area. They spread a sheet of fine linen between him and the people. He washed (sanctified) his hands and feet and then undressed. רבי מאיר says: he undressed and then washed his hands and feet. He went down and immersed, came up and dried himself. They brought him the white garments. He dressed and washed his hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a new משנה. It describes, step by step, the כהן גדול's second טבילה of יום הכפורים and his change into the white garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This טבילה took place inside the holy area (בית הפרוה), and a linen sheet was put up for modesty. The תנא קמא says he washed his hands and feet before undressing. רבי מאיר says he undressed first. Everyone agrees he washed his hands and feet again after putting on the white garments.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber in the עזרה where the כהן גדול immersed
Washing (sanctifying) the hands and feet from the כיור
The white linen garments for the special יום הכפורים service

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
They brought him to the Hall of Parva,
and it was in the holy area.
phrases.notes: It was inside the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: They spread a sheet of fine linen
between him and the people,
he sanctified his hands and feet, and undressed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: פָּשַׁט, קִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he undressed, then sanctified his hands and feet.
phrases.notes: The disagreement is only about the order.

phrases.english: He went down and immersed, came up and dried himself.
They brought him white garments,
he dressed and sanctified his hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of heating the מקוה and opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second טבילה was done in בית הפרוה behind a linen sheet. The תנא קמא and רבי מאיר disagree about whether washing the hands and feet came before or after undressing.

steps.title: How much the morning and afternoon linen garments were worth
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about the value of the כהן גדול's morning and afternoon linen garments. These were paid for by the public, and he could add from his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the morning he wore Pelusium linen worth twelve מנה. In the afternoon he wore Indian linen worth eight hundred זוז. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: in the morning he wore garments worth eighteen מנה, and in the afternoon garments worth twelve מנה, thirty מנה in total. These were paid for by the public. If he wanted to add more, he added from his own money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues by describing the value of the linen garments the כהן גדול wore on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the morning garments were more expensive than the afternoon ones. For רבי מאיר, 12 מנה plus 800 זוז (8 מנה) comes to 20 מנה. The חכמים say 18 plus 12, which is 30 מנה. The community paid this basic amount, and the כהן גדול could add his own money for finer garments.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine linen from Pelusium in Egypt
A unit of money equal to 100 זוז

steps.confusionAlert: 800 זוז equals 8 מנה, since a מנה is 100 זוז. So in both opinions the morning garments cost more than the afternoon ones.
steps.whatToRemember: The second טבילה took place in בית הפרוה. The white garments were expensive: 20 מנה in total according to רבי מאיר and 30 מנה according to the חכמים. The public paid, and the כהן גדול could add from his own money.

phrases.english: In the morning he would wear
Pelusium linen worth twelve maneh.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם הִנְדְּוִיִין שֶׁל שְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת זוּז,
phrases.english: In the afternoon, Indian linen worth eight hundred zuz,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בַּשַּׁחַר הָיָה לוֹבֵשׁ שֶׁל שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: in the morning he would wear garments worth eighteen maneh,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם שֶׁל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה,
phrases.english: and in the afternoon garments worth twelve maneh,
thirty maneh in total.
These are paid by the community,
and if he wants to add, he adds from his own money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה by describing the white garments mentioned in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר says the garments were worth 12 מנה in the morning and 800 זוז in the afternoon. The חכמים say 18 מנה and 12 מנה (30 in total). They were paid from public funds, and the כהן גדול could add from his own money.
